summary: Verified first: no RSVP screen read rsvpDeadline — only good-to-know's day-line, the Settings editor and spec fixtures did — so the six strings were right by coincidence alone. They now interpolate {{deadline}}, computed by the three consuming screens (rsvp-create, rsvp-edit, delegate-edit) from the PUBLIC config the app already loads at the root — no fetch added — via a new rsvpDeadlineLabel(deadline, lang) helper, reactive to both a config change and a runtime locale switch. Formatter: Intl.DateTimeFormat (day numeric + month long), safe in all three locales because every hard-rule-4 target ships full en/es/fr CLDR data and it needs none of Angular's registerLocaleData machinery (the app registers no locale data, so DatePipe would throw for es/fr). en maps to en-GB ('1 May', the day-first form the shipped copy used), es-ES gives '1 de mayo', fr-FR gives '1 mai' with one documented exception — French writes the first of a month as an ordinal and Intl has no ordinal-day support, so day '1' renders '1er', exactly the shipped form. Calendar date taken in Europe/Madrid (ADR-0029 §4.2). Asserted per T391's method: live (the create screen must render the FIXTURE's date, '1 September' — a date no locale file ever carried) and off disk (six keys x3 locales carry {{deadline}} and no month name). Proven to bite: fixture set to 2026-10-15, live test fails on the rendered '15 October'; restored, green. Scope fence held: six keys, nothing else. Gates: unit 654 → 662, e2e 460 → 470, 440/0/30.

acceptance.criterion: The six strings take the deadline as an interpolated parameter from the wedding configuration, formatted for the active locale — not typed into a locale file. The RSVP screens read rsvpDeadline from the config they already load; do not add a fetch.
acceptance.evidence: The task's premise was verified before any change: grep over src/** shows rsvpDeadline read only by shared/good-to-know (the day-line, ADR-0046 §4), config-manager (the Settings editor) and spec fixtures — no RSVP screen. The six keys (rsvp.create.attending.subtitle, rsvp.edit.seatsHeld.none/.singular/.plural, rsvp.edit.declinedSub, rsvp.hub.detail.declinedSub) now carry {{deadline}} in es/en/fr — 6 replacements per locale file, nothing else touched (git diff: 12 changed lines per file, all six keys). The three consuming screens compute it as `rsvpDeadlineLabel(configurationService.weddingConfigPublic()?.rsvpDeadline ?? '', translateLanguage.currentLang())` — ConfigurationService is the root singleton whose constructor already loads GET /v1/config/public for every visitor (the same signal app.html gates route content on), so injecting it adds zero HTTP calls; rsvpDeadline is a required field of WeddingConfigPublicResponseDto.
acceptance.notes: The computed reads two signals, so the rendered date follows both a config refresh and a runtime language switch — the delegate-edit and rsvp-create specs assert the config half by writing a new deadline into the stubbed signal and watching the rendered copy change without recreating the component.

acceptance.criterion: Locale-correct formatting, and nothing else locale-dependent. Say in the report which formatter you used and why it is safe in all three locales.
acceptance.evidence: Formatter: Intl.DateTimeFormat with { day: 'numeric', month: 'long', timeZone: 'Europe/Madrid' }, locale-mapped en→en-GB, es→es-ES, fr→fr-FR (src/app/core/helper/rsvp-deadline-label.ts). Why it is safe in all three: (a) every browser hard rule 4 names — iOS Safari and Chrome Android current — ships complete CLDR month/day data for en, es and fr as part of ECMA-402, so there is nothing to load or polyfill; (b) it bypasses Angular's DatePipe deliberately, because DatePipe requires registerLocaleData for es/fr and this app registers none — DatePipe would throw for two of the three locales; (c) the mapped locales reproduce the shipped forms exactly: en-GB '1 May' (day-first, matching the copy and the British guests; bare 'en' resolves en-US and flips to 'May 1'), es-ES '1 de mayo', fr-FR '1 mai'. One documented exception: French typography writes the FIRST of a month as an ordinal ('1er mai') and Intl has no ordinal-day support, so a day-part of '1' is mapped to '1er' via formatToParts — only ever the first, since other French dates carry no ordinal ('15 mai', asserted). The calendar date is taken in Europe/Madrid, the timezone every other date judgement in the app uses (hub ADR-0029 §4.2, todayInMadrid), so the stored UTC-midnight deadline cannot render as the previous day for a guest abroad — unit-tested at the boundary (2027-04-30T23:00Z → '1 May'). An unparseable value returns the raw string rather than leaving a hole in the sentence.
acceptance.notes: Nothing else became locale-dependent: the change interpolates one date into six existing sentences; identifiers remain untouched (hard rule 19a governs a different class and no identifier is involved here).

acceptance.criterion: Assert it, per T391's method: a test that the rendered string carries the configured deadline and not a hardcoded month. Prove it bites by changing the fixture's deadline and watching it fail.
acceptance.evidence: e2e/rsvp-deadline.spec.ts, two halves per T391's live+off-disk pattern. LIVE: sign in as a guest with a pending RSVP (the same manual flow design-parity-rsvp.spec.ts uses — the post-login redirect lands on /rsvp), assert the create-step subtitle contains 'Please reply by 1 September.' — the interpolation of the fixture's CONFIG_PUBLIC.rsvpDeadline (2026-09-01), a date no locale file ever carried, so it can only have come from the configuration — and does NOT contain 'May'. OFF DISK: all six keys in all three locales must contain {{deadline}} and no month name, with an accent-aware matcher (\b cannot bound 'août'), so the date cannot be typed back into a locale file without failing the suite. PROVEN TO BITE exactly as the bullet specifies: api-mocks.ts rsvpDeadline changed to 2026-10-15T00:00:00.000Z → the live test fails ('Please reply by 1 September.' not found; the screen renders '15 October'); fixture restored → 2/2 green. Unit layer additionally asserts the rendered copy in all three screens and that a changed configured value changes it (rsvp-edit, rsvp-create, delegate-edit specs).
acceptance.notes: The three screen specs' local copy fixtures were updated to the shipped {{deadline}} shape — those fixtures exist precisely to mirror the shipped keys' structure, and the pre-existing assertions ('1 seat held.') now assert the full deadline-bearing sentences against a stubbed public config.

risks.risk: The initial bundle's transfer size is 195.62 kB against the hub's < 200 kB gzipped budget — 4.4 kB of headroom — and the raw-byte warning (808.59 kB vs 500 kB) has been firing unremarked for some time (already 803.05 kB before this session; the consent-service comment records 494.84 kB in 2026-08). Every task that touches the root bundle eats the margin invisibly because the raw-byte warning has become noise nobody reads.
risks.surfaces_at: The next few kB of root-bundle growth crosses the hub budget silently; angular.json's raw-byte thresholds measure a different thing than the hub's gzip target (a mismatch the consent-service comment already flagged in T252). Worth its own small task: align the budget config, or at least reset the raw threshold so the warning means something again.

risks.risk: The French '1er' ordinal is a hand-mapped exception on top of Intl (formatToParts day '1' → '1er'). If the deadline is ever displayed elsewhere with a bare Intl call, the two renderings diverge on the one date French treats specially.
risks.surfaces_at: Any future surface that formats rsvpDeadline as prose — it should call rsvpDeadlineLabel, which the helper's doc block says.

risks.risk: good-to-know's day-line still renders its own deadline-adjacent copy through a separate path (ADR-0046 §4 variants); this task did not touch it, per the scope fence. If its locale strings ever carry a literal date the same defect returns one surface over — the off-disk e2e guard covers only the six RSVP keys.
risks.surfaces_at: T394's triage covers the broader class; a generalized 'no month name in any locale value that also has a configurable-date sibling' rule is one of its candidate proposals.
